newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy court of accounts urges early welfare reform.
newsitem.headline: Italy court of accounts urges early welfare reform.

text.p: The head of Italy's Court of Accounts, which oversees state accounts, urged the government on Wednesday to address crucial welfare spending reforms by drafting legislative changes before the summer.

Court of Accounts president Giuseppe Carbone told a joint budget commission of the upper and lower houses of parliament the government should speed up draft delegate laws so they would not affect debate on 1998 budget legislation later this year.
This would avoid too many decisions having to be taken when parliament came to examine the 1998 budget law, which he said was a measure more for shorter term economic policy.
The budget must be presented to parliament by the end of September and approved by both chambers by the year end.

The centre-left government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi is striving to reach a three percent budget deficit to gross domestic product ratio required by the end of this year to join Europe's single currency proposed for January 1999.

Italy's European Union partners are concerned it will not be able to sustain that ratio into 1998 and Italy is under pressure to carry out longer term reforms to its welfare spending, particularly in the state pension system.

However the government faces heavy resistance to welfare spending cuts both from trade unions and the Refoundation Communist party, whose support is crucial to Prodi in the lower house of parliament but which has proved an uneasy ally in the past.
